q: ID3 keeps how many hypotheses during search?

All trees consistent with the data

q: Because ID3 does not backtrack, it can:
options: Settle on a locally optimal tree
Never produce a consistent tree
Only use one attribute
Not handle more than two classes
explain: An early greedy choice is never revisited, so a better overall tree may be missed.

q: How many distinct Boolean functions are there of 3 Boolean attributes?
explain: There are 2³ = 8 possible inputs, and each can map to 0 or 1, so 2⁸ = 256.

q: ID3 uses all training examples at each step. A benefit is that:
options: Decisions are statistical, so it is less sensitive to a few errors
It trains on one example at a time
It needs no memory
It always reaches zero error on test data
explain: Choosing by a statistic over many examples means single errors have less influence.
